appraisal_events.evidence: Mme de Marsantes était considérée dans le faubourg Saint-Germain comme un être supérieur, d'une bonté, d'une résignation angéliques ... elle enthousiasmait le faubourg Saint-Germain ... À la campagne, Mme de Marsantes était adorée ... C'était, disait-on, la parfaite chrétienne.
appraisal_events.explanation: Society's collective voice elevates Mme de Marsantes as a near-saintly, universally admired figure, both in the faubourg and in the countryside.

appraisal_events.evidence: des femmes ... vénérées comme d'idéales saintes de vitrail, avaient fleuri sur la même souche généalogique que des frères brutaux, débauchés et vils ... comme étaient le duc de Guermantes et Mme de Marsantes; Être grande dame, c'est jouer à la grande dame ... jeu qui coûte extrêmement cher; Mme de Marsantes agaçait un peu dans la conversation ... ce que les personnes moins brillantes ... raillaient comme de la stupidité.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator complicates the collective admiration by linking Mme de Marsantes genealogically to her disreputable brother the duc de Guermantes, and by exposing her celebrated simplicity and formality as a costly, class-conditioned performance that privately irritates more discerning observers.

status_effects.explanation: Her standing is genuinely elevated by the near-unanimous admiration of her social world, both in Paris and in the countryside.
The narrator's ironic exposure of her performed simplicity, her kinship with her brutal brother, and the private irritation her mannerisms provoke somewhat undercut the surface picture of sainthood.

ambiguities: The narrator's overall stance toward Mme de Marsantes is deliberately unresolved: he registers genuine, widespread admiration for her while also exposing performative and class-conditioned aspects of that image, without the passage settling clearly on either an endorsed or purely ironic reading.
